chapter: Dreamland and the Tuxedo dance hall
title: The Easter shooting between the Tuxedo and 101 Ranch rivals
summary: Harry Parker and Billy Phillips are killed in a gun fight on Easter, and Manetta recalls climbing off the bandstand and Joe Oliver's place next door.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Who was being shot? Who was being shot? Who was shot? Who all was shot?
Well, Harry Parker got killed. Billy Phillip got killed.
Who killed him? Drip the blood.

Drip the blood. Boy, Brooks, flowers, you know. He's the one when his wife started off, he killed Billy Phillip. And the other Charlie, they were shot, injured. And Drip the blood, he was shot. He ran through the hall, ran across the street. We happened to get off the bandstand. I didn't want to, I take the rope. I said, well, I'm going to tie this rope to the piano. He says, tie it to the piano. Tie it any way. And come on down the rope. There was Peter. Oh man, look at the contract. He was praying, saying his rosary. Well, he saw them, they were running. They were running. So we happened to get on the stand. It goes out the back. The back door under the balcony? Not, huh? Was there a back door under the bandstand? Sure. The back door you go out the back of the building.
And you go right out to Liberty Street, right opposite the corner there. It was Groshearts where Joe Aller was playing.

So, see the people running over that way. Let's go by Joe's. that way. Let's go by Joe's. We went by Joe's, I'll see the excitement there, was a drip of blood. He had ran, shot, and he went and fell in that place, in Groeschel's. Fell down, laying on the floor. Pick him up, brought him down the last. Well, he got over it, yeah.

You mean he wasn't killed? No, he wasn't killed. I don't understand who was, was it two rival gangs or something? Two rival dance halls there, yeah, Tuxedo 101. Yeah. So the boys from the 101 came over to the Tuxedo? Yeah, the boss. The boss. The boss. The boss. They're the Phillips. Oh, yeah. He got killed. He got. What did he expect to do when

they came over to the Tuxedo? Well, you know, he just got ties. How many people went to the Tuxedo? Oh, the raid was there, man, and it was run different, and he was a man with fight. He was losing business. He was losing business.
Taking his girls away from him and all the entertainers. Sure. Were these girl entertainers?

No, these girls, Jeffers girls, working there and dancing, sell beer, so much off beer, and things like that, you know. And so, well, it looked like they were all flocking to Tuxedo Hall because it was a fine, big place, and they had a swell band. And Billy didn't like that very much? Well, no, that was an arraignment man. So they were all killed, both sides? Yeah. So Charlie, he was shot. Charlie Parker, he was shot, but he got over it, too. Who was he? That shot, that was Harry's brother. Oh, I see. Harry, Harry and Billy, they got instantly killed.
Instantly killed? Yeah. No musicians got hurt in this? No, no musicians got hurt.
Well? That must have been some night. Oh, that was on Easter Sunday morning. Easter Monday morning. What year was it? Easter Monday morning.
We can look it up. It's in 1917 or so about.
